title: Does the parts file hold the offsets inline, or point at per-file .saidx files?
body:
1. Inline. One read opens the whole aggregate. One edited part rewrites all of it.
2. By reference. Each part keeps its own `.saidx` and the parts file carries paths, stamps and counts alone. It stays small and a stale part rebuilds by itself. Cost: N + 1 files and N opens.

Lean: by reference. The case for inline is the one to make if opening a thousand files turns out to cost more than rebuilding them.

The type's name follows from the answer: a type that only points at per-file indexes should not be named as if it held offsets.
